newsitem.title: UK: IBCA assigns individual rating of D to Seoul Bank.
newsitem.headline: IBCA assigns individual rating of D to Seoul Bank.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Tuesday it had assigned an individual rating of D to Seoul Bank (SB).

"The bank's previously assigned legal rating of 2 remains unchanged, reflecting IBCA's view that the Korean authorities would not allow the failure of any of the country's major banks," the agency said in a statement.
IBCA said SB was one of South Korea's "big five" commercial banks and shared many features in common with its peers among the former government-owned large commercial banks.
The rating agency noted SB's low profitability and poor asset quality, arising in large measure from government-directed lending in earlier years.
"The bank's Individual rating of D reflects these problems which, in the case of SB, have been compounded by an above average exposure to Korea's troubled construction industry," it said.
"In the first half of 1996, SB's performance was the weakest among its peers, burdened by high loan loss provisions and large securities valuation losses," IBCA said.
"Like other Korean banks, SB trades actively in stocks and is currently suffering some adverse effects from the poor performance of the Korean stock market," it said.
